key_insight: A MicroUS-specific self-supervised foundation model ({micro}FM) improved prostate image analysis performance, especially when training labels were scarce.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce annotation burden and help build more accurate automated tools for prostate capsule, urethra, and lesion analysis in micro-ultrasound workflows.
method: Pretrained on 1,736,391 unlabeled MicroUS images from 780 patients using DINOv2-style self-supervised learning.
Fine-tuned and tested on prostate capsule segmentation, urethra segmentation, and prostate cancer lesion localization.
Compared against randomly initialized models and foundation models pretrained on natural, medical, and ultrasound images.
evidence_signal: With 10% of training scans, {micro}FM reached Dice scores of 93.8% for capsule segmentation and 58.4% for urethra segmentation, and about 0.75 sensitivity at two false positives per 3D volume for lesion localization.
watch_item: The pretraining was retrospective and single-institution, and the model did not explicitly use 3D modeling.
paper_title: Data-Efficient Prostate Micro-Ultrasound Image Analysis using a Modality-specific Foundation Model
